designationHistory.indexText: President Coolidge added public land to the Medicine Bow National Forest, Wyoming, and set the added area aside as a game refuge and breeding place for game animals and birds.

authority.citation: Proclamation of Aug. 8, 1924, 43 Stat. 1964 (under Act of June 7, 1924, ch. 307, 43 Stat. 594)

designationHistory.note: Neither the act nor the proclamation uses the name Sheep Mountain; they describe townships 14 and 15 north, range 77 west. The link to Sheep Mountain rests on a secondary account (wyoachs.com), which says the refuge came from a bill by Sen. John Kendrick and Coolidge's proclamation, and on the Land Areas Report, which lists Sheep Mountain Game Refuge on the Medicine Bow.
